text:
Adrian Kempe has been one of the best process stories on a Kings team that has lost four straight. At five on five, Los Angeles has had 59.72% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 13.29 points better than without him, and he's taking 1.47 expected goals per hour of his own, well above his 1.06 last season.

The goals haven't matched. He has 6 on 8.4 expected, and three of them came in one night against San Jose on November 4. Outside that hat trick, his last ten games produced nothing on 5.0 expected goals, and the team has also scored 6.0 fewer than expected with him on. That's the profile of a player due for a run, not one losing his touch: 56 shots in 17 games, 6 power-play points, and EDGE speed bursts in the 94th percentile.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him as a defensive cost, with opponents getting more with him on. This year's on-ice numbers point the other way, which is the thing to watch as the sample grows.
headline: Adrian Kempe is driving play, not the scoresheet
